newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-CHILE CLOSER TO WORLD CUP, BOLIVIA AND ECUADOR FADE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHILE CLOSER TO WORLD CUP, BOLIVIA AND ECUADOR FADE.

text.p: Chile hopes of reaching next year's World Cup in France rose enormously while the chances of Bolivia and Ecuador took a severe dent following the weekend's South American qualifiers.

Chile, who beat hammered the fading Colombians 4-1 in Santiago Saturday, leapfrogged Ecuador, Bolivia and Uruguay in the South American qualifying group after Sunday's results also went in their favour.

Ecuador dropped two precious points as they were held 1-1 away to lightweights Venezuela in the oil city of Maracaibo while Bolivia, beaten finalists in the Copa America last week, lost 2-1 to Peru, who kept on Chile's tail.
The Chileans, the group's highest goalscorers, jumped into fourth place with 16 points and play four of their remaining five games at home where they have a 100 percent record.
Paraguay, who suffered their first home defeat in four years as they went down 2-1 to Argentina, stayed top with 23 points, but their lead over Argentina was reduced to one point.

Paraguay, Argentina and Colombia, who have 18 points, look fairly certain of a place in France next year as the top four teams in the group qualify. However, after Saturday's debacle, Colombia, who have taken one point from their last five games, know that any more slip-ups could be fatal.

Chile's win before a 75,000 crowd in Santiago was set up by a first-half hat-trick by Marcelo Salas. Two of his goals were created by striker Ivan Zamorano, who also converted a last minute penalty for his 10th goal of the qualifiers.
Peru's win in Lima kept them level on points with Chile, although in addition to having played a game more, their goal difference is worse than their neighbours by 10.
German Carty and Jose Soto put Peru two goals ahead, although Bolivia could have forced a draw. They pulled one goal back through Luis Cristaldo and missed an excellent chance to equalise.

Bolivia's chances of reaching a second successive World Cup now look increasingly remote, as they have 14 points and only one home game left. They will probably pay the penalty for dropping too many home points in La Paz, where the 3,600 meters altitude gives them a huge advantage.
Ecuador were left with 15 points after conceeding an equaliser eight minutes from time against Venezuela, who had only taken two points from their previous 11 games.

In a game between the only two South American nations never to have played in a World Cup, Ivan Hurtado gave Ecuador a 55th-minute lead on a bumpy pitch but Gabriel Miranda hit back to shatter their dreams.

"We expected more. We expected to win. The situation has become more complicated with this result," said Ecuador's Colombian coach Francisco Maturana. "But while there's a chance, we must keep on fighting."

In Asuncion, Argentina ended Paraguay's 100 percent home record in the qualifiers with first half goals by Marcelo Gallardo, whose free kick crept in at the near post, and Juan Veron. Roberto Acuna replied with a second-half penalty.
Gallardo atoned for his Copa America performance, where he took four penalties and missed two.

Paraguay were severely depleted, with goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert, their captain and driving force, serving the second of a four-match suspension and injures to key players Francisco Arce, Miguel Benitez and Catalino Rivarola.
The absence of the menacing figure of Chilavert, who rates Argentina as his favourite enemies, clearly lifted a burden off the backs of the Argentine players.
Paraguay, Chile, Bolivia and Uruguay have five games left and the other teams four.
